empiricalEvidence.uncertainty: Discord documents no grammar. Its docs have one example header, in the legacy 24/6/27 shape. The current 24/6/38 and 26/6/38 widths rest on dated empirical reports (2022-2024) and third-party regexes, never on either pinned scanner. Segment 1 width follows from base64 of an 18- or 19-digit ID, which is arithmetic, not a stated rule. Discord gives no stability guarantee, and a maintainer-issued token has not been measured here.

supportedContexts: Authorization: Bearer <uuid> on a line naming api.heroku.com
HEROKU_API_KEY=<uuid> in env, shell export, compose/YAML env
Terraform provider "heroku" { api_key = "<uuid>" } on one line
git remote https://:<uuid>@git.heroku.com/<app>.git
same line as a case-insensitive heroku keyword
single-line .netrc: machine api.heroku.com login <email> password <uuid>
empiricalEvidence.uncertainty: The bare lowercase 8-4-4-4-12 UUID shape rests on one provider changelog example plus peer rules; Heroku states no grammar in prose, whether it ever issued uppercase hex is unknown, and no legacy token can be newly issued, so issuance cannot be re-observed. A UUID carries no marker of its own and is structurally identical to Heroku app/release/request ids and to current UUID-shaped secrets (OAuth client secret, refresh token), so the value is only claimed beside a heroku keyword.

release_evidence.reason: The Release run (36610474587) itself succeeded end to end -- qualification, both crates, all nine PyPI files, all ten npm packages, registry-install verification on all eight Node targets and Chromium, and 'Tag verified release' all passed. A Reconcile Release dry run (36613259577) afterwards found every npm package, both crates, and every PyPI file already published with content matching this source revision and published nothing, so no real reconcile was needed or run. The run's 'Record release manifest' job, however, carried the registry_state snapshot that the 'Publish npm dependency linux-arm64-musl' job took immediately after its own publish, before npm:@redact-secret/node-linux-arm64-musl had propagated on the npm registry, so that one package is recorded 'unpublished' (and its artifact_digests 'published' shasum is null) even though npm records the version as published at 2026-09-29T18:30:17Z and the same run's own later 'Verify registry install aarch64-unknown-linux-musl' job installed 0.1.0-beta.11 from the registry and passed. This is the same npm registry propagation-lag false negative documented in the beta.3/beta.5/beta.6/beta.10 records, not a partial publication. This record corrects that one registry_state entry to 'published', fills that package's 'published' shasum from the live registry (the same value the Reconcile dry run reported as matching), and adds the release_evidence this repository's manifest job does not itself populate (tag, per-registry checksums, workflow run references, clean-install verification), assembled from the run's own artifacts plus registries independently checked live on 2026-09-29. Every other field is the workflow's own output, preserved verbatim as original_manifest.

bare three-segment token anywhere on a line, quoted or unquoted
env/JSON/YAML/TOML/compose/Actions assignment and client.run("...") argument
startup log line, Markdown text
empiricalEvidence.uncertainty: Discord documents no grammar. Its docs have one example header, in the legacy 24/6/27 shape. The current 24/6/38 and 26/6/38 widths rest on dated empirical reports (2022-2024) and third-party regexes, never on either pinned scanner. Segment 1 width follows from base64 of an 18- or 19-digit ID, which is arithmetic, not a stated rule. Discord gives no stability guarantee, and a maintainer-issued token has not been measured here.

empiricalEvidence.uncertainty: The bare lowercase 8-4-4-4-12 UUID shape rests on one provider changelog example plus peer rules; Heroku states no grammar in prose, whether it ever issued uppercase hex is unknown, and no legacy token can be newly issued, so issuance cannot be re-observed.
